faqs.question: What should a 13-year-old boy be for Halloween?
faqs.answer: Pick something built on clothes he already owns with one clear joke, such as an NPC with a paper name bar or a PE teacher in a zipped tracksuit. Both take about 10 to 15 minutes, cost an estimated US$1 to US$2 and keep his face visible, which most school rules require.

faqs.question: What costumes can teen boys wear to a school costume day?
faqs.answer: Choose one with the face showing, no make-up and nothing carried in the hands, because strict districts such as Davis School District in Utah ban all three. Hats are usually fine, so a valet, a lumberjack without the axe or a 1920s newsboy all pass.

faqs.question: Can I bring a toy gun with my costume to school?
faqs.answer: No, not at the schools quoted here. Cleveland Charter High School in Los Angeles bans real, replica or fake guns and knives, and Surrey Schools in British Columbia bans weapons including fake ones, even as part of a costume.

faqs.question: Does an orange tip make a toy gun legal to carry?
faqs.answer: The US federal rule in 15 CFR Part 272 only requires toy and look-alike guns to carry a blaze orange marking when they are made, sold or shipped. It does not override a school ban, and it does not cover BB, paintball or pellet guns at all.

faqs.question: Can he wear a mask to school for Halloween?
faqs.answer: Often not. Davis School District bans masks outright, while Cleveland Charter High School allows one only at a lunchtime spirit activity and never one that completely hides who the student is.

faqs.question: My son says he is too old for costumes. What can he wear?
faqs.answer: Suggest a costume that is mostly his normal clothes plus one detail, like a ski instructor's goggles or a wrestling champion's card belt. Low-effort costumes tend to stay on longer than ones built around a mask or a big prop.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Costume Ideas for Teen Boys That Pass School Rules

The Halloween costume ideas for teen boys that work start from clothes they already own, keep the face showing and carry no prop that looks like a weapon. Below are 15 of them in four budget tiers, from under US$5 to under US$40 (estimates, October 2026), each marked for whether it passes a strict school day.

Teen boys also tend to decide late: on SubhSandesh, 49.4% of Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages were built on the festival day itself, a different festival and a small sample (n = 89). Where the photo ends up matters too, since 48.3% of the pages shared on our site are opened on a phone. Below: the 15 ideas, three real school rules, the toy-gun question and a cost table.

## What makes a costume wearable for a teen boy?

A wearable teen-boy costume is one he keeps on all evening: built on his own clothes, recognisable within a few seconds, with his face visible and his hands free. If he has to lift a mask every ten minutes, it comes off by 8 pm.

School adds a second test. Davis School District in Utah [bans masks, make-up and any hand-held accessory "real or pretend"](https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1696628038/davisk12utus/tnjjupkhdihlvvbsy3uk/HalloweenGuidelines.pdf) on costume days, while hats and crowns are allowed. Every idea below is written so the school version works under those rules, with the after-school extras listed separately.

Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027. With no school on either date, check your school's notice for which weekday, if any, is costume day.

## 15 Halloween costume ideas for teen boys, by budget tier

Every bullet gives the look, a school-day verdict, a cost estimate and a build time. Costs are October 2026 estimates (EST) for new or thrifted basics; clothes he already owns are not counted.

### 1. Already in his wardrobe: 4 costumes, est. under US$5

- **PE teacher:** tracksuit zipped to the chin, socks pulled up to the knee, a whistle on a lanyard and a cap. *School day: yes, the whistle is worn, not carried · est. US$2 for the whistle · 10 minutes.*
- **Barbecue dad:** cargo shorts over joggers, socks with sliders, and an apron lettered GRILL SERGEANT in marker. *School day: yes, tongs stay home · est. US$3 for the marker · 15 minutes.*
- **NPC (non-player character):** a plain grey hoodie, a paper name bar on a headband reading "Townsperson_12", and one line he repeats all day. *School day: yes · est. US$1 · 15 minutes.*
- **Ski instructor in October:** puffer jacket, beanie, goggles parked on top of the beanie and a paper lift pass on the zip. *School day: yes, goggles stay up so the face shows · est. US$0–5 · 10 minutes.*

### 2. Under US$15: 4 costumes, est. 20–60 minutes

- **Valet parking attendant:** a thrifted waistcoat, a clip-on bow tie and a lanyard of paper car keys labelled with ghost number plates. *School day: yes · est. US$10–12 · 30 minutes.*
- **Wrestling champion:** a dressing gown with his name taped across the back, a headband, and a gold card belt worn round the waist. *School day: yes, the belt is worn · est. US$8 for card and gold paint · 1 hour.*
- **Lumberjack on his day off:** flannel shirt, beanie, braces and boots, with no axe. *School day: yes, and the missing axe is the joke · est. US$8–12 for braces · 20 minutes.*
- **Retired superhero:** a sweater-vest, slippers, a bedsheet cape safety-pinned at the shoulders and a felt chest letter that has started to peel. *School day: check, as some schools ban capes in corridors · est. US$6 · 45 minutes.*

### 3. Under US$40: 3 costumes, est. 1–3 hours

- **Loan shark:** a thrifted suit jacket and tie under a grey shark-head hood that leaves the face open, with a paper "rates" card in the breast pocket. *School day: yes, face open · est. US$25–35 · 1 hour.*
- **Claw machine:** a box painted as an arcade cabinet with a clear front, a few soft toys inside and a claw made from a coat hanger. *School day: no, too wide for desks and doorways · est. US$15–25 · 3 hours.*
- **1920s newsboy:** flat cap, braces, rolled trousers and a shoulder satchel of paper "EXTRA: HOUSE ON ELM ST HAUNTED" sheets. *School day: yes, the satchel is worn · est. US$20–30 thrifted · 1 hour.*

### 4. With three or four mates: 4 group costumes, est. per person

- **Kitchen brigade:** head chef, line cook, dishwasher and waiter in whites and aprons from home, with name tapes. *School day: yes, with no knives, not even plastic ones · est. US$5–10 each · 20 minutes.*
- **Barbershop quartet:** card straw boaters, striped shirts or waistcoats, bow ties and felt moustaches, plus one rehearsed 30-second song. *School day: yes, hands free · est. US$8–12 each · 1 hour.*
- **Haunted-house removal crew:** matching T-shirts lettered "Spectral Removals" and one friend under a white sheet as the client being moved out. *School day: the sheet hides a face, so the ghost goes sheet-off at school · est. US$5–8 each · 30 minutes.*
- **Bobsled team:** matching tracksuits, bike helmets and numbered bibs, walking in a line inside a cardboard sled. *School day: no for the sled, yes for the tracksuits · est. US$10–15 each · 2 hours.*

## What do school dress codes say about masks, props and make-up?

School costume rules come down to three tests: can staff see his face, does anything resemble a weapon, and does it mock a group. Three published policies show how strict that gets.

- **Davis School District, Utah:** no masks, no make-up, no hand-held accessories "real or pretend (i.e., wands or weapons)"; hats and crowns allowed.
- **Cleveland Charter High School, Los Angeles:** [masks may not completely obscure the student's identity](https://www.clevelandhs.org/apps/pages/index.jsp?uREC_ID=33131&type=d&pREC_ID=1309504), may be worn only at a lunchtime spirit activity, and props may not include "real, replica, or fake guns/ knives/other weapons".
- **Surrey Schools (School District No. 36), British Columbia:** a [28 October 2024 notice](https://www.surreyschools.ca/_ci/p/179320) says weapons "including fake ones" are not allowed even as part of a costume, and flags violent imagery such as a hangman's noose.

That rules out most masked film killers as school costumes. Surrey also flags costumes built on race, culture, religion, gender-swapping for mockery or ableism.

After school, a mask is a judgement call for him, but the eyes are the part worth keeping visible. In a 2024 trust experiment, [faces with only the top half showing were judged as trustworthy as full faces](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11164842), while faces showing only the bottom half were judged less trustworthy.

## Why doesn't an orange tip make a toy gun school-safe?

US federal rules require a toy, look-alike or imitation firearm to carry [a blaze orange plug at the muzzle](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-15/subtitle-B/chapter-II/subchapter-H/part-272), recessed no more than 6 millimetres, or another approved marking. That rule governs selling and shipping, not schools. It also excludes BB, paintball and pellet guns, which is what most realistic airsoft props are.

So the orange tip changes nothing on a school day: Cleveland Charter and Surrey both ban replicas and fakes by name. A 2015 case report in the *International Journal of Adolescent Medicine and Health* describes a high-school student who [brought a concealed toy gun into school after the Sandy Hook shooting](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25411993) a case the authors use to discuss how clinicians should evaluate adolescent forensic behaviour (abstract only read).

The practical rule: if the costume needs a gun, knife, bat or sword to make sense, pick another one for school. Leave realistic props at home after dark too.

## Teen boy costume tiers compared

The table sets the four tiers side by side on cost, build time and school-day pass rate. "Strict" means Davis-style rules: no masks, no make-up, nothing hand-held.

| Tier | Est. cost per person (Oct 2026, EST) | Build time | Pass a strict school day as built |
|---|---|---|---|
| Already in his wardrobe | US$0–5 | 10–15 min | 4 of 4 |
| Under US$15 | US$6–12 | 20–60 min | 3 of 4 (cape depends on school) |
| Under US$40 | US$15–35 | 1–3 h | 2 of 3 (claw machine too wide) |
| Group of 3–4 | US$5–15 each | 20 min–2 h | 2 of 4 fully; 2 need a school version |

The wardrobe tier is the safest at school as well as the cheapest, because nothing in it needs a hand-held prop or a face covering. The group tier fails most often, usually on one bulky shared piece.

## Sending a costume photo to one person

Plenty of teen boys wear the costume but never post it. A private link for one chosen friend or grandparent is lower stakes than a public feed. On SubhSandesh, 38.5% of creators password-protect their page before sharing it.

Our [interactive Halloween card with a haunted house to explore](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about 5 minutes, holds up to six photos and ends with a 1080×1920 Boo License showing the costume he picks for them. If he wants more, the [cinematic premium Halloween page with a voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about 10 minutes and adds a voice note up to 60 seconds, up to 12 photos and a reply box.

Both are one-person greeting pages with partner, bestie, family and kids modes. They are not party invitations and not a costume shop. For a different occasion, [browse every SubhSandesh template](https://subhsandesh.in/templates).

## When to skip this list

These 15 ideas are built for a strict school day, so they use clothes, not effects. A 16-year-old who wants a screen-accurate masked character for a haunted-house attraction should follow that venue's rules.

Policies differ by district and country: Davis bans make-up outright while Cleveland Charter allows a mask at lunch. Read the notice your own school sends home.

Our cards lose too. For a whole party, a group chat beats a one-person link, and the template interface is in English only.

- Cleveland Charter High School (Los Angeles). *Halloween Costume Guidelines and Resources* (undated). [clevelandhs.org](https://www.clevelandhs.org/apps/pages/index.jsp?uREC_ID=33131&type=d&pREC_ID=1309504)
- Surrey Schools, School District No. 36. *Halloween Costume Guidelines*, 28 October 2024. [surreyschools.ca](https://www.surreyschools.ca/_ci/p/179320)
- 15 CFR Part 272, *Marking of Toy, Look-Alike and Imitation Firearms* (57 FR 48453, 26 October 1992; amended 23 January 2013). [eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-15/subtitle-B/chapter-II/subchapter-H/part-272)

- Rice TR, Hoffman L. Taking a toy gun to school. *International Journal of Adolescent Medicine and Health*, 1 May 2015 (abstract only). [Europe PMC](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25411993)
